geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the existing clipped subtraction into a directional notch that can articulate the west access edge more clearly.
Point the notch to the program-mapped access side.
Increase the opening width to make the threshold feel public rather than incidental.
Extend the cut vertically so the entry void has enough sectional presence to read in the four-view diagram.

rationale: The candidate reads as one primary elongated mass with a secondary lifted/bridged threshold, so it is coherent across the four views and not merely a box. The west-access logic is partially responsive: the lift creates a recognizable ground-level seam/undercut on the access side, which suits neighborhood_living better than a sealed edge. The silhouette is acceptable but only moderately resolved; the form is still somewhat stair/clip-like and the stepped notch feels more like a subtraction than a spatially generous public court. Compared with the references, it aligns most with the courtyard/terrace bar language and with bridge-linked mixed-use masses, but it is less open and less sectionally expressive than the strongest precedents. Program fit passes because the mass can plausibly support a compact mixed-use building with active ground edge and one clear void, though it would benefit from a more legible carved public space and a cleaner section/roof relation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion-like and sculpturally scalloped than this candidate; do not copy the roof profile.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single low-rise mass with a carved central void and a bridge-like upper connector can make a clear neighborhood/public threshold without needing tower logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger multi-building composition; candidate is a single compact mass, so only the court logic transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a courtyard can support neighborhood mixed-use if the ground void remains legible and public.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more open and transparent; candidate is more closed and heavier at the base.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: An elongated low-rise bar with a central void and strong horizontal spread fits a neighborhood program well.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more distributed and landscape-driven; the candidate should not become a campus cluster.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, connected low-rise wings and bridge elements can preserve continuity while creating public open space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference has more articulated wings and void depth than the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes around a courtyard and elevated connections can keep a compact mixed-use mass readable.

warnings: Parcel containment appears respected in the image set; no hard-gate rejection on containment.
The access-edge response is present but modest; the ground void could be more public and spatially continuous.
The form is close to a generic bar with local clipping, so it risks reading as over-trimmed rather than deliberately sectioned.
